text.p: Diana, Princess of Wales, said she was devastated on Tuesday by news of the killing of fashion designer Gianni Versace.
In a statement issued from the South of France where she is on holiday, she said: "I am devastated by the loss of a great and talented man."
Diana made an exception to her preference for British designers to wear Versace and often spoke of her friendship for him.
The designer paid tribute to the princess by naming a handbag after her -- The Lady Di.
The princess bought clothes from the designer's ready-to-wear and couture collections. She often visited his shop in London's Bond Street.
But their friendship was strained this year when the princess pulled out of a book venture with the designer.

Diana had agreed to write the foreword for a book Rock and Royalty, but she pulled out after she discovered that pictures of the royal family were to be used alongside of semi-nude models in bondage gear.
British fashion designers were quick to pay tribute to Versace.
1960s fashion icon Mary Quant said: "He was all about life. His designs were immediately recognisable as rich, glamorous and sexy.
"He dared to use a strong dash of vulgarity just beautifully. He was a man who everyone adored."
Punk queen Vivienne Westwood said: "He was obviously one of the most talented and famous designers of the last few years."
Rock star Elton John, no stranger to Versace's creations, was too upset to make a public statement after hearing the news on holiday in Nice, south of France.
"He's completely shocked and numb with disbelief about the whole thing," a spokesman said.
Earlier this year the singer wore a Versace evening gown for a photo-shoot.
British actress Elizabeth Hurley, who owed her first real fame to Versace, said in statement: "Gianni was a dear friend of mine and I am going to miss him horribly."
A black dress, slashed almost to the navel and held together with safety pins, propelled Hurley from obscurity to the front pages when she wore it to the premiere of "Four Weddings And A Funeral".
